title: Remove authenticator
purpose: Confirm removal of one lost sign-in factor from an account.
summary: Confirm removing one lost sign-in factor from an account.

tasks.title: Remove the factor
steps: Check the factor named on the page.
If [[Confirm it is you]] is shown, type your own password in [[Your password]], and a code from your authenticator app if it asks for one.

good_to_know: Only this factor goes. The account, its roles and its other factors stay.
The removal is recorded in the account's audit history. If that record cannot be written, nothing is removed.
The owner can enroll a new factor from their own Two-factor authentication pages. If the laboratory requires one of them, their next sign-in sends them to set one up first.
Removing asks you to confirm it is you (your password, a code, or both, as the page asks), unless you confirmed in this browser in the last 5 minutes.
Where this deployment sends email, the owner is emailed that an administrator removed the factor, whatever they chose on Email notices.

sections.title: Access and displayed scope
paragraphs: Requires an active account with both Staff and Superuser status. A laboratory admin role, Staff status alone or individual authenticator or email-address model permissions granted to a user or group do not open this page.
The page names the factor type and shows a summary of what will be removed: this single factor record. There is no bulk removal from the list.

items.label: Yes, I’m sure
items.description: Once you have confirmed it is you (see Confirm it is you), removes the factor. In the same step the account’s audit history records who removed it, when, and the factor’s type, enrollment and last-use times. The secret is never recorded. If the audit record cannot be written, nothing is removed.

sections.title: Confirm it is you
paragraphs: Yes, I’m sure asks you, the person signed in, to confirm it is you, unless you already confirmed in this browser in the last 5 minutes. A Confirm it is you section then appears above the buttons, and nothing is removed until what you type there is accepted. Signing in does not count: only confirming again does, and a new sign-in, even in the same browser, starts without one. Once you have confirmed, no page that asks (account administration, and the session limits and second sign-in factor rule on Security settings) asks again in this browser for 5 minutes. A page opened while you were confirmed asks when you select Yes, I’m sure after the 5 minutes have passed.

Confirming on Confirm your password, or with a code before a change to your own two-factor settings, counts too, once every factor your account has was given there within the last 5 minutes: each counts for 5 minutes from when it was given, so the earlier one runs out first. A confirmation here counts for those pages as well. A new password, or a new or different authenticator app, on your account since you confirmed makes the next removal ask again, for both. An account with neither a password nor an authenticator app cannot confirm, so it cannot remove a factor until it sets a password.

When the confirmation is missing or not accepted, nothing is removed, and no audit event or administration history entry is written. A password or code not accepted is listed in your own Sign-in history as Re-authentication failed and counts toward the failed sign-in limit; an attempt that limit refuses is listed as Too many failed attempts. What you type under Confirm it is you is never stored, logged or put in an audit event.

items.label: Your password
items.description: Shown when your account has a password: your own current password, not the factor owner's. The help under it says what removing asks for and that you are not asked again in this browser for 5 minutes. Left empty: Enter your password to save this change. Not accepted: Incorrect password. Accepted, but the code is not: Enter your password again with the code (the page does not keep it).

items.label: Authenticator or recovery code
items.description: Shown when your own account has an authenticator app: a code from it, or one of your unused recovery codes, which is then used up. Left empty: Enter a code from your authenticator app, or a recovery code, to save this change. Not accepted: Incorrect code. The password is checked first; when it is not accepted, the code is not checked and can still be used.

items.label: Too many failed login attempts. Try again later.
items.description: The failed sign-in limit refused your password or code before checking it, after too many that were not accepted. Wait a few minutes, then try again.

items.label: Too many attempts to confirm it is you. Wait a minute, then try again.
items.description: Shown after 10 tries within a minute by your account (the Confirm your password pages count too). Nothing was checked, and the refusal is not listed in Sign-in history.

items.label: Your account has no password to confirm it is you, so this change cannot be saved. Set a password on Change password first.
items.description: Your account has neither a password nor an authenticator app, so it has nothing to confirm with. Set a password from Change password in the account menu, then try again.

items.label: Your sign-in factors changed, or your confirmation ran out, while this page was open. Confirm it is you again.
items.description: An authenticator app was added to or removed from your account, or your confirmation ran out, while the removal was being checked. Nothing is removed. The section now asks for what your account has: fill it in and select Yes, I’m sure again.

sections.title: Effect
paragraphs: Only this factor is removed; the account, its roles and its other factors stay. Removing an authenticator app leaves any Recovery codes record in place, and removing recovery codes leaves the app. Self-service deactivation cleanup is not run. The owner can enroll a new factor from their own Two-factor authentication pages.

Sessions the owner has open are not ended by the removal. Where the laboratory's second sign-in factor rule (Security settings) covers the account, the owner's next sign-in without an authenticator app goes to Set up a second sign-in factor before anything else, so removing a lost app is how the owner gets to add a new one. End the account's sessions from its page here to apply that at once.

In the same change, the removal records one email notice to the account's owner: an administrator removed the authenticator app (or the recovery codes) from their account, when (UTC), and whom to contact if they did not expect it, the laboratory's security contact as recorded on its profile or its administrator. It holds no code, secret or address. It is sent where the deployment sends email, whatever the owner chose for their email notices, and not when the account is inactive or has no email address when it is sent; with email off it is recorded as not sent.

sections.title: Navigation
paragraphs: Home, application, model list and object breadcrumbs return to the permitted maintenance pages.
